title: Teams case chat sync
use_case: Post a card to a Teams channel when a case is created, changes status, severity, assignee or title, or gets a comment, with the tenant name, the case's details, key findings, recommended next steps, latest comments and a link to the case. Optionally, with the library's chat bridge, people in the channel can set the status or comment from Teams.
trigger: Platform Events, source Case, events Create, Update and Comment Added. Leave When does this playbook run? at Always; the playbook's own settings do the scoping. It can also run by hand from a case.
connections: Taegis.MicrosoftTeams 1.2.4, the Microsoft Teams connector Sophos manages, set to a Teams Workflows webhook URL
Taegis.Case 1.0.5, the case connector Sophos manages, to read the case
requires: Microsoft Teams with Workflows, and Sophos Fusion playbooks under Security Operations > Automations. The chat bridge is optional: only two-way replies need it, plus a Teams outgoing webhook.
mdr_note: Sophos MDR doesn't run or watch this playbook, and it doesn't change what Sophos MDR does. With Managed by at any, Sophos MDR cases are posted too, comments included, so check who is in the channel.
rollback: None for posted cards. Turn the playbook off to stop posting.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: This playbook posts a card to a Teams channel when a case is created, changes status, severity, assignee or title, or gets a comment. The card carries the tenant name, the case's details, key findings, recommended next steps and latest comments with a link to the case, and goes through the Microsoft Teams connector Sophos manages, set to a Teams Workflows webhook URL. The chat bridge is optional and only adds two-way replies from Teams.
notes:
Testing: - Every version passed playbookValidateDSLV2 with no errors or warnings: 1.0.0 on 2026-10-21, 1.1.0 to 1.2.1 on 2026-11-04, 1.2.2 on 2026-11-15, 1.2.3 and 1.3.0 on 2026-11-16 (us01 and eu02). - On 2026-10-21 a run by hand with a person's comment as its input posted the comment's text. - On 2026-10-22 a renamed copy posted three cards to a real Teams channel through a Workflows webhook (HTTP 202): a reopened case and two status changes made through the chat bridge. The bridge's [chat-sync] comments fired it too, and it skipped them. - On 2026-11-04, on the same test tenant, 1.1.0 ran on a status change and on a new comment and posted two cards to the Teams channel, which the webhook accepted with HTTP 202. Each card showed case details, key findings, recommendations and the three latest comments, without the bridge's [chat-sync] comments or the comment the card was about. - For 1.1.1, on 128 Markdown key findings from two test tenants, ITDR finding cases included, Sophos Fusion's own CEL evaluator rendered key findings and recommendations exactly as the repo's tests do, and no card kept a
, a # heading line or a whole paragraph in bold. - A renamed copy of 1.1.1 on the first test tenant posted a card for a new comment (HTTP 202). Run by hand with a Comment Added event marked internal, in the shape the platform documents (case.delta.comment.isInternal), it posted nothing. - A renamed copy of 1.2.0 on the first test tenant posted two cards (HTTP 202) with a Tenant row and an Open in Sophos Fusion button: one for a status change, where the event named the tenant, and one run by hand, where it read the tenant name through the case connector. - For 1.2.1, on 128 key findings from two test tenants, 107 with tables, Sophos Fusion's own CEL evaluator matched the repo's tests and no card kept a raw tag or table row. Run by hand on both tenants, it posted cards (HTTP 202), one with a made-up comment of HTML and tables. - On 2026-11-15 1.2.2 posted a card in us01, and the execution log held no entry for the post, so no webhook URL. - On 2026-11-16, on a Sophos MDR tenant in us01, two status changes posted 1.2.3 cards (HTTP 202) whose reply line named in_progress and customer_action_required. - On 2026-11-16 1.3.0 there posted Approval needed cards for requests on a Low severity case and skipped the bridge's notes. 1.3.1's card, read from the execution log, showed the request ID, expiry and both reply lines under the headline. Known gaps: - The webhook's 202 doesn't show how Teams draws a card. example.png is a 1.2.1 card from a real case on a second test tenant, as Teams showed it. - Key findings saved as rich text are left out; every case on the test tenant had Markdown or none. - The Create event is untested, because the Cases API refused to create a test case. - No real internal comment has fired the playbook: the test tenant's API credential can't add one, as only partner users can, so the internal check was tested with a hand-run event.
